```sh
kafka config set <names...>
```

Set one or more config entries on a resource

## Arguments

| Argument   | Description              |
| ---------- | ------------------------ |
| `names...` | resource names to update |

Shared options and defaults: [connection profiles, JSON output, logging and help](../../../global-options/).

## Defaults

Applies the provided key/value entries to the selected resources; use --dry-run for validation.

## Before you run

Changes resource behavior; some broker settings need a restart while dynamic settings apply immediately. Save existing overrides and validate the change before execution.

## Flags

| Flag                               | Description                                                           |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--brokers <string>`               | comma-separated broker list, e.g. localhost:9092                      |
| `--type <string>`                  | resource type: topic, broker, broker-logger, client-metrics, or group |
| `--entry <key=value> (repeatable)` | a config entry to set, key=value (repeatable)                         |
| `--dry-run`                        | validate without changing anything                                    |

## Examples

```sh
kafka config set --type topic orders --entry retention.ms=604800000
kafka config set --type topic orders payments --entry cleanup.policy=compact --dry-run
```

## Output

Illustrative, abbreviated output. Empty arrays show the result envelope; actual entries, identifiers, optional fields and broker errors depend on the request and cluster.

With `--json`:

```json
{
  "results": []
}
```

Declared exit codes: `0`, `1`, `2`, `4`. See the exit-code reference for meanings.
